newsitem.title: UK: London freight - Owners find some optimism.
newsitem.headline: London freight - Owners find some optimism.

text.p: Despite some weak nearby fixtures, owners generally sounded more optimistic about freight market prospects, particularly for April, brokers said.
Congestion and delays are still prevalent in western Canada and Brazil (compounded by strikes) and shipping schedules are thus being pushed back in these areas.
Caper brokers reported healthy fresh demand for April positions, and panamax brokers believed that a support level has now been reached east and west.
The decline of the Baltic Freight Index (BFI) was almost arrested, with the index falling just three points to 1,414.
GRAIN - Panamax grain fixtures from the U.S. Gulf were steady. Two stems of 54,000 heavy grain were reported fixed for end March at an unchanged $24.00 no combo.
Lorentzen and Halla, for example, who have first half April enquiries on this route were said to be willing to consider repeating this level.

South American panamax grain rates were broadly steady, although Halla fixed Meridian Sky 64,293 dwt delivery Plate about March 20/25 trip south Korea at a poor $12,750 daily plus a $270,000 ballast bonus. This vessel was said to be committed to drydocking in the Far East.

Following ADM's fixture of Sun P for 55,000/5 heavy grain Paranagua/Rotterdam at $15.00, there was talk that Cereol had booked Seaeagle for 50,000/5 heavy grain Paranagua/Spanish Med at $17.00 with an Adriatic option at an additional $2.25.
Both vessels loading on prompt dates (and built 1981).
In the east, Egyptian charterers booked Top Trader 69,338 dwt delivery Japan trip via Australia redelivery Egyptian Med at a solid $7,950 daily.
New grain orders included Toepfer with 2.6/2.8m cft Mississippi/Spain or Portugal for March 12/19 and 25,000 barley up river Plate/Turkey March 17/25.
Others included, Safmarine for a panamax delivery river Plate end March for three to five or four to six months, redelivery Atlantic or Far East.

Dreyfus for 54,000 heavy grain U.S. Gulf/Taiwan April 2/9, Glencore 25,000 barley Rouen/Tunisia prompt, Continental 25,000 wheat Necochea/South Africa March 13/23, and andre 45,000 heavy grain Paranagua/Lisbon for March 21/31 (ideas $14.00 with tonnage said to be indicating $14.50).
Little emerged in the handy-sizes other than talk that Tradigrain had booked a vessel of about 25,000 dwt with prompt delivery north France for a trip to Umm Qasr.
MINERALS - Coal and ore trading picked up, although with mixed rate levels reported.
However, there was some optimism among owners/brokers that April might fulfil the promise not often achieved of March loading positions.
Cape Eagle 161,000 dwt was fixed at a firm $18,000 daily by Navix delivery Dunkirk mid-March for a trip via Hampton Roads and Richards Bay to Japan.
Some rates for older vessels remained weak. Enemm took the 20-year old Pawnee for 100,000 iron ore Nouadhibou/Gijon for March 15/25 at only $3.70.
Giic was said to have booked Narvik/Bahrein at $10.10 for early April.
China Steel was understood to have fixed about 150,000 tonnes iron ore Tubara0/Kaohsiung, and Carbunesti 171,000 dwt open Kaohsiung March 20 was believed fixed on subjects.
Reports circulated that Diamond Sea was booked by Bao Shan for 130,000 tonnes iron ore west Australia/Qingdao for April at $6.00, but some brokers reckoned the rate was up to a $1 less.
The 1982-built Marine Courage 127,000 dwt agreed 16 to 18 months timecharter delivery Ireland end March with Cobelfret at $10,000 nett daily but failed on subjects.
Panamax trading was more active in the east, although details of a number of fixtures have yet to emerge.
British Steel have been linked with Clymene 63,325 dwt for a trip from Australia to UK.

The Koula L 71,730 dwt prompt shanghai was thought to have been fixed on subjects, and both Legiony Polskie 73,505 dwt and Panaghiotis L 64,166 dwt were also said to have been fixed from Far East positions.
HANDY-SIZES - Details of some Atlantic timecharter fixtures were not disclosed. For example, Magda P 34,194 dwt from east coast south america.
Another was Tradigrain's booking of a 25/30,000 dwt vessel from the Continent to Umm Qasr.
Fednav was said to be working tonnage in the Atlantic and Far East for period timecharter to cover the lakes season, but details were also kept confidential.
Brokers reported firmer conditions for modern geared tonnage in the Far East.
BIFFEX futures closed 35 to 50 points firmer after trading 143 lots. The most active month of March saw 63 lots done and traded last at 1,460, up 45 points.
